primary_sources: Attention Is All You Need Transformer Architecture

rules.explanation: Relying on legacy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) or LSTMs for modern natural language tasks creates severe sequential bottlenecks and limits long-range context handling.
rules.do: Implement transformer-based architectures utilizing multi-head self-attention mechanisms to process input tokens in parallel and capture complex contextual relationships across long sequences.
rules.dont: Do not build large-scale language generation pipelines on outdated sequential recurrent architectures that fail to scale with modern hardware.

rules.explanation: Inefficient tokenization algorithms (such as naive word or character splitting) inflate sequence lengths, waste computational tokens, and degrade cross-lingual performance.
rules.do: Utilize subword tokenization algorithms (e.g., Byte-Pair Encoding [BPE], WordPiece) optimized to balance vocabulary size, token compression ratios, and rare word handling.
rules.dont: Do not use unoptimized raw-string splitting or excessively large, sparse vocabularies that degrade inference memory efficiency.

rules.rule_name: Context Window Management and KV Cache Optimization
rules.explanation: Failing to manage token context windows and Key-Value (KV) cache memory leads to out-of-memory errors and excessive latency during long text generation.
rules.do: Optimize context window allocation, implement sliding-window attention or efficient KV caching strategies, and prune redundant conversational history before feeding prompts to LLMs.
rules.dont: Do not dump unbounded historical message logs directly into model context limits without truncation or summarization wrappers.

rules.rule_name: Model Decoding Parameters and Temperature Tuning
rules.explanation: Using arbitrary or uncalibrated decoding hyperparameters (Temperature, Top-p, Top-k) results in either overly repetitive, robotic text or highly hallucinatory, erratic outputs.
rules.do: Tune decoding parameters systematically based on use case requirements: low temperature (0.0 - 0.2) for deterministic tasks (code, extraction) and moderate temperature (0.7 - 0.9) for creative synthesis.
rules.dont: Do not leave LLM generation parameters at uncalibrated default values across diverse production use cases.
